plan.contextChunk: This figure is a heavily labeled diagram of a hyperbola opening left and right, centered at the origin of a coordinate system with arrowhead-tipped axes marked x at the right and y at the top. Two dark blue branches sweep away from the horizontal axis, one on each side. A pair of orange dashed lines cross at the center and run diagonally to the corners of the drawing, each tagged by a leader arrow reading "Asymptote" at the lower left and lower right. A teal dashed rectangle is centered on the origin, its vertical sides passing through the turning points of the two branches and its horizontal sides passing through two points on the vertical axis, with its corners sitting on the orange diagonals. A short red segment along the horizontal axis joins the two turning points and is labeled "Transverse axis" by an arrow pointing down onto it; a light blue segment along the vertical axis joins the top and bottom of the rectangle and is labeled "Conjugate axis." Dark blue dots at the ends of the red segment are each labeled "Vertex," light blue dots at the ends of the vertical segment are each labeled "Co-vertex," teal dots farther out along the horizontal axis are each labeled "Focus," and an orange marker at the crossing point is labeled "Center." Assembling every named element on one curve shows how the rectangle and its extended diagonals govern the directions the branches approach.

interactionPlan.concept: For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, a sets the vertices along the transverse axis and b sets the co-vertices along the conjugate axis; together they build a guide rectangle whose extended diagonals are the asymptotes the branches approach.
elements: Horizontal x-axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'x' at the right end
Vertical y-axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'y' at the top
Dark blue right branch of the hyperbola opening rightward, turning at (a, 0)
Dark blue left branch of the hyperbola opening leftward, turning at (-a, 0)
Two orange dashed asymptote lines y = ±(b/a)x crossing at the origin and extending to the corners of the drawing
Teal dashed guide rectangle centered at origin with corners at (±a, ±b), its vertical sides tangent to the branch turning points and corners lying on the orange diagonals
Short red segment on the x-axis from (-a,0) to (a,0) — the transverse axis
Light blue segment on the y-axis from (0,-b) to (0,b) — the conjugate axis
Dark blue vertex dots at (±a, 0)
Light blue co-vertex dots at (0, ±b)
Teal focus dots at (±c, 0) with c = sqrt(a²+b²)
Orange marker at the origin — the center
Leader-arrow labels: 'Conjugate axis', 'Transverse axis', 'Co-vertex' (top and bottom), 'Vertex' (left and right), 'Focus' (left and right), 'Center', 'Asymptote' (lower left and lower right)
Optional readout of the standard equation x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 with current a and b values

interactions.label: a — half transverse axis (vertex distance)
interactions.teaches: a is exactly where each branch turns: widening a slides the vertices and the red transverse axis outward and flattens the asymptote slope b/a.

interactions.label: b — half conjugate axis (co-vertex distance)
interactions.teaches: b never touches the curve, yet it sets the rectangle's height and therefore the asymptote slope, so it controls how steeply the branches open.

interactions.label: Construction guides
interactions.teaches: The rectangle and its diagonals are scaffolding, not part of the hyperbola — but the branch shape is completely determined by them.

demo_steps.title: The labeled hyperbola
demo_steps.narration: Start with the full figure: center at the origin, vertices on the red transverse axis, co-vertices on the light blue conjugate axis, foci farther out, and orange dashed asymptotes through the corners of the teal rectangle.

demo_steps.title: Guides alone
demo_steps.narration: Hide the curve. All that remains is a rectangle of half-width a and half-height b plus its extended diagonals — enough information to predict the entire hyperbola.

demo_steps.title: Stretch a: move the vertices
demo_steps.narration: Increase a. The vertices and the red transverse axis slide outward, the rectangle widens, and the asymptotes become shallower, so the branches pull apart and open more gently.

demo_steps.title: Stretch b: steepen the opening
demo_steps.narration: Now grow b with a fixed. The vertices do not move at all, but the taller rectangle steepens the diagonals and the branches flare open more sharply.

demo_steps.title: Curve only
demo_steps.narration: Turn the guides off. The same branches remain, now clearly hugging the invisible diagonals — the construction has vanished but its fingerprint is the curve's shape.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: a says where the hyperbola starts (the vertices) and b says where it is headed (the asymptote slope b/a) — the branches never touch the co-vertices, yet b fully controls how they open.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Centered Cartesian axes with double arrowheads, thin black, 'x' label at right, 'y' at top, roughly square drawing area about 6 units in each direction. Hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 drawn as two thick dark navy branches opening left and right. Orange (coral) dashed lines of slope ±b/a from corner to corner through the origin. Teal dashed rectangle with corners at (±a, ±b), its vertical sides touching the branch vertices and its corners exactly on the orange diagonals. Short thick red segment between the vertices on the x-axis; thin light blue segment between the co-vertices on the y-axis. Dot colors: navy vertices, light blue co-vertices, teal foci at ±sqrt(a²+b²), small orange square/asterisk at the center. Black thin leader arrows from outside text labels to their targets, mirroring the original placement: 'Conjugate axis' and 'Co-vertex' upper left/top, 'Transverse axis' and 'Center' upper right/bottom center, 'Focus' and 'Vertex' on both left and right flanks, 'Asymptote' at lower left and lower right. Show a small live equation readout x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 with the current numeric a and b. When 'Curve only' is selected, fade out the rectangle, diagonals, focus dots, and construction labels while keeping the branches and axes fixed; when 'Guides only', hide the navy branches.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for transverse axis length: the learner moves the vertices outward or inward, the red axis and hyperbola branches update, and a sets where each branch turns.
- Slider for conjugate axis length: the learner changes the rectangle height, the asymptote slopes and branch openings update, and b controls the guide rectangle that determines approach directions.
- Toggle between guide rectangle and final curve: the learner switches the dashed rectangle and asymptotes on and off, the branches remain in place, and the role of the construction guides in shaping the hyperbola becomes clear.

authoredContext:
As with the ellipse, every hyperbola has two axes of symmetry. The transverse axis is a line segment that passes through the center of the hyperbola and has vertices as its endpoints. The foci lie on the line that contains the transverse axis. The conjugate axis is perpendicular to the transverse axis and has the co-vertices as its endpoints. The center of a hyperbola is the midpoint of both the transverse and conjugate axes, where they intersect. Every hyperbola also has two asymptotes that pass through its center. As a hyperbola recedes from the center, its branches approach these asymptotes. The central rectangle of the hyperbola is centered at the origin with sides that pass through each vertex and co-vertex; it is a useful tool for graphing the hyperbola and its asymptotes. To sketch the asymptotes of the hyperbola, simply sketch and extend the diagonals of the central rectangle. See the figure.

Key features of the hyperbola

This diagram illustrates the various components of a hyperbola centered at the origin, including the vertices, co-vertices, foci, transverse axis, conjugate axis, asymptotes, and the rectangular box used to construct the asymptotes.

In this section, we will limit our discussion to hyperbolas that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane; the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. We will consider two cases: those that are centered at the origin, and those that are centered at a point other than the origin.

discrepancies: Line weights/saturation differ: the source's asymptotes and guide rectangle are bold, strongly saturated orange and teal dashes, while the generated ones are thinner and paler, making the construction guides read as secondary rather than co-equal with the curve.

The generated branches and asymptotes run all the way to the canvas edges (and the asymptotes extend past the drawn branch ends at top-left/top-right), whereas the source crops both to a tidier extent with the dashed lines slightly overshooting the branches.
Focus dots are drawn noticeably smaller than the vertex/co-vertex dots; in the source all marker dots are of comparable size, so the foci are less prominent than in the original.

Minor leader-line differences: the source's 'Conjugate axis' arrow terminates at the center crossing point, while the generated one terminates partway up the blue segment; similarly the 'Center' arrow is shorter than in the source.
evaluation.notes: A near drop-in replacement for the source: all marks (navy branches, red transverse axis, blue conjugate axis, teal dashed rectangle, orange dashed asymptotes, orange center asterisk, foci/vertices/co-vertices) and all ten leader-arrow labels are present and cleanly placed, backed by genuinely useful a/b sliders, a guide-visibility toggle and a five-step guided demo; only stroke weights, marker sizing and curve extents deviate slightly from the original.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all scores are near-maximal, with only trivial cosmetic deviations that do not warrant another iteration.
